newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-SELES BRINGS HAPPY MEMORIES TO FED CUP VENUE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SELES BRINGS HAPPY MEMORIES TO FED CUP VENUE.

text.p: Monica Seles, haunted by dark memories in recent years, was positively ebullient at the prospect of playing the Fed Cup final for the United States on the court where the black clouds finally lifted for her some 14 months ago.

"I have really unbelievable memories from the convention centre so it's really special to be back here," Seles said of the seaside building where the United States will try to wrest the Fed Cup from three-time defending champions Spain this weekend.

It was at the convention centre in July 1995 that Martina Navratilova coaxed Seles out of seclusion for an exhibition match -- her first since the horrific stabbing that took place during a match in Hamburg in April 1993.

Seles's first steps back into the public eye and into a competitive tennis match in Atlantic City ended more than 27 months of exile, largely spent suffering from emotional trauma that lingered long after her physical wounds had healed.
"It was unbelievable when I first played against Martina here," recalled Seles.

"It's hard to believe it was a year and a month ago," said the 22-year-old Seles, who has since been to two U.S. Open finals and won the 1996 Australian Open. She is ranked co-number one in the world along with Steffi Graf.
"When I heard they were coming back I was really excited and very happy. Everything is just really positive going into the matches and I think we all hope that we can just carry the momentum."

Seles will get the first chance to translate that momentum into results when she opens the tie Saturday against Conchita Martinez, who has teamed with Arantxa Sanchez Vicario to win four Fed Cup finals -- three from the United States.

The presence of Seles is what makes the United States favourites to beat the Fed Cup team of the '90s. She holds a combined 21-1 career record against the Spanish duo, including very recent wins over each of them.
"That's what our team wanted so it's a good sign," said U.S. captain Billie Jean King Friday after Seles was drawn to play the first match both days.

Olympic champion Lindsay Davenport will play the second singles match each day and then team with U.S. Fed Cup veteran Mary Joe Fernandez for Sunday's potentially deciding doubles match against Martinez and Sanchez.
There, fitness could play a big role with Davenport and Martinez playing doubles immediately after their second reverse singles.
Davenport has a losing record against both Spaniards, but is buoyed by her Atlanta Olympic triumph over silver medalist Sanchez.
"It helps knowing that I have beaten her in the past and that I'm capable of it," Davenport said. "I know I can win. Hopefully, if I'm hitting the right shot, I will win."
A very relaxed Miguel Margets, captain of the Spanish team appearing in its sixth consecutive final, said the pressure is on the home team.
"The U.S. needs this victory more than us," Margets said. "We have won three times in a row and we are playing out of our country against a great team.
"It's USA who needs this victory because its their third consecutive final, they have no title and they know this is a great opportunity."
Seles just made her Fed Cup debut in July's semifinals against Japan. But Fernandez has come up empty in three trips to the finals and Davenport has been on the short end twice.

"It means a lot to me because for a couple of years now we've almost done it and haven't done it, so I don't know what it feels like to win it," Davenport said. "I know what it feels like to lose it. Hopefully it will change this time."
Sanchez, a dominant force in Fed Cup play for nearly a decade, seemed to be relishing Spain's new role as underdogs.
"That aspect can help us. They are more favourites and that's good for us," she declared. "We feel good. We're ready."
Added Martinez: "We're ready for anything. We're going to play our best."
